## Natural history notes

A large black swallowtail butterfly characterized by dark wings with rows of yellow spots, blue scaling on the hindwings, and orange eyespots near the tails; females are usually darker with more blue, while males have brighter yellow bands. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, prairies, pine flatwoods, parks, and other sunny open habitats where nectar plants and carrot-family host plants occur. Adults feed on nectar from many flowers, while the caterpillars feed on plants such as dill, fennel, parsley, carrot, and native members of the carrot family, often showing bold green, black, and yellow banding as they grow.
